boundaries: Distinguish point from arc elasticity, nominal from real aggregates, stocks from flows, and accounting identities from behavioral equations.
No elasticity forecasts, demand predictions, policy recommendations or equilibrium claims.
Ceteris-paribus assumptions must be explicit, never hidden.
Monetary-policy reaction functions, econometric estimation and forecasting models are excluded.
Index-number records must state basket, base period and formula (Laspeyres/Paasche/Fisher) exactly as sourced.
coverage_guidance: Priorities are seeds, not a finite checklist. Continue into adjacent source chapters/subtopics inside the boundaries, selecting independently reusable relationships. Save multiple bounded batches without waiting for owner review. Check supplied inventory and prior returns for equivalent relationships and conflicting IDs. Record out-of-format discoveries as deferred with exact sources and missing capabilities; do not force chains or dilute quality for a quota.
integration_expectation: Mostly dimensionless ratios and currency sums; meanings (elasticity, gdp_component, growth_rate, break_even_quantity and similar) are new and require extension. All seed forms are scalar + - * / ** and fit the engine once meanings exist. Never relabel an elasticity as a discount rate or an aggregate as an operating cost to force execution.
mission: Curate atomic, reusable deterministic economics relationships: elasticities, growth rates, national-accounting identities and break-even/cost arithmetic, each with explicit scope and measurement conventions. Continue through successive review batches during the sustained session; no forecast chain or policy use case is required. This is descriptive formalization, not forecasting or policy advice.
priorities: Point price elasticity of demand as a ratio of relative changes
Midpoint (arc) elasticity between two observed price/quantity points
GDP expenditure identity (C+I+G+NX) as an accounting definition with component meanings
Compound annual growth rate between two dated levels
Break-even quantity from fixed cost, unit price and unit variable cost
special_checks: Retain elasticity signs (demand elasticity is normally negative); never absolutize silently
Reject zero-quantity and zero-price denominators explicitly
Growth-rate base year and period count must be explicit; test a zero-growth boundary
Break-even records must guard price above unit variable cost; identities must balance in references by independent recomputation, not by repeating the identity
starter_sources: https://www.bea.gov -- navigate to GDP concepts and the NIPA handbook for the expenditure identity; the root alone proves nothing
https://www.bls.gov -- navigate to CPI concepts for index-number background; the root alone proves nothing
Find an accessible principles-of-microeconomics/macroeconomics textbook (for example an OpenStax economics title) for elasticity and growth-rate definitions; record exact book, edition and section
title: Economics: elasticity, aggregates and deterministic accounting
